text:
His paintings would not be so valuable

now

if he had not

cut off his ear

put that rag around his head

and then killed himself

among the corn stalks.

would the poems of that other one

be so famous if he had not

disappeared at 19,

left everything to go

traffic arms and look for gold

in Africa only to

die of syphilis?

what about the one who was

murdered on the road

by Spanish fascists?

did that give

his words more

meaning?

or take that one who was a

national hero

those iceberg symphonies rising

cutting that particular sky

in two

he had everything handed to him

then he worried about old age

decided to save his head

went home

disappeared and was never seen

again.

what strange behavior, didn't someone say

once?

that a man must be as durable as his

art, that is what they expect, they demand the

impossible: creation and creator being the

same. this is the dirty trick

of every age

translation.title: Beethoven Conducted His Last Symphony Completely Deaf
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The title is retained despite the poem's allusive body; the source does not establish a title-body mismatch.
